newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-TIGER WOODS SUES FRANKLIN MINT OVER UNAUTHORIZED MEDAL.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER WOODS SUES FRANKLIN MINT OVER UNAUTHORIZED MEDAL.

text.p: Golf sensation Tiger Woods filed a lawsuit Tuesday against the Franklin Mint for the unauthorised use of his likeness on a commemorative medal it was selling.
According to the lawsuit, filed in U.S. District Court here, Woods is seeking a court order that would force the company to destroy any medals still in stock and to pay him unspecified damages.
The lawsuit names Franklin Mint as well as its owners, Stewart and Lynda Resnick.

According to the complaint, Franklin Mint officials tried to get Woods's permission to use his likeness on a medal to commemorate the 21-year-old star's record-setting Masters victory, but it was refused.

The defendants, however, ran advertisements in major newspapers selling the souvenir medal "honoring golf's new master" for $37.50. The ads created the "false impression that Tiger Woods is in some manner associated or affiliated with the medal," the complaint said.

Woods, who has enjoyed a meteroic rise to the top of the golf world since turning professional last year, has struck multi-million dollar endorsement deals with a select group of companies, including Nike, Rolex and American Express.
"Tiger has been extremely careful about the use of his name and image for commerical purposes and we don't want people to think these items are authentic," Hughes Norton, his manager said.

Woods's press agent issued a statement saying the young golf star's representatives explicitly told Franklin Mint that "its products were inconsistent with the overall marketing plan and image for Woods."
